extraction.name: Panoptic Segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series with Convolutional Temporal Attention Networks
extraction.description: We present the first end-to-end, single-stage method for panoptic segmentation of Satellite Image Time Series (SITS). We also introduce PASTIS, the first open-access SITS dataset with panoptic annotations.
extraction.creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot, Loic Landrieu
extraction.publisher: LASTIG, Univ. Gustave Eiffel, ENSG, IGN
extraction.rai:dataCollection: PASTIS is comprised of 2,433 sequences of multi-spectral images of shape 10×128×128. Each sequence contains between 38 and 61 observations taken between September 2018 and November 2019, for a total of over 2 billion pixels. The dataset spans over 4000 km², with images taken from four different regions of France. Annotations are taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The time between acquisitions is uneven with a median of 5 days. This lack of regularity is due to the automatic filtering of acquisitions with extensive cloud cover by the satellite data provider THEIA.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentinel-2 satellite images after atmospheric correction and re-sampling at a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel. The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of Sentinel-2.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automatic filtering of acquisitions with extensive cloud cover by THEIA. We opt to not apply further pre-processing or cloud detection, and produce the raw data in PASTIS.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each pixel of PASTIS is associated with a semantic label taken from a nomenclature of 18 crop types plus a background class. Each non-background pixel also has a unique instance label corresponding to its parcel index. All annotations are taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control over 98% and the relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Crop mapping entails major financial and environmental stakes: remote monitoring of agricultural parcels is necessary for fair allocation of agricultural subsidies (over 50 and 22 billion euros per year in Europe and the US, respectively) and for ensuring best crop rotation practices.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The combination of ambiguous borders and hard-to-classify parcel content makes for a challenging panoptic segmentation problem.
